papers.title: Somnus, a tunable, open-source platform for automated EEG sleep scoring in physiological and disease mouse models.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: Introduces Somnus, an open-source Python package for automated rodent EEG/EMG/video sleep staging, built on a base model trained across recordings from six laboratories and designed for rapid user-guided fine-tuning on uncertain epochs. It enables accurate custom sleep scorers for disease models with minimal manual correction without requiring whole-cohort hand-scoring.

papers.title: Isoflurane anesthesia CNS recovery state: ultra-slow oscillations and cellular-stress-responsive gene expression.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: Compared recovery from 4 h isoflurane anesthesia with time-matched sleep and sleep deprivation in mice using EEG/EMG and frontal cortex RNA-seq, finding that isoflurane recovery produced transient arousal rebound, reduced and fragmented NREM/REM sleep, and persistent ultra-slow oscillations normalizing within two weeks. Transcriptomics showed isoflurane enriched integrated stress response and unfolded protein response genes, distinct from sleep deprivation, indicating anesthesia recovery is neurophysiologically and molecularly distinct from restorative sleep.

papers.title: Interfloor noise triggers sleep fragmentation and affective deficits via dysregulation of the orexin-serotonin axis and hippocampal synaptic plasticity.
papers.summary: In male C57BL/6 mice exposed to simulated interfloor noise (70-100 dB, 12 h daily for 7 days), the authors report sleep fragmentation with selective REM sleep reduction, anxiety-like behavior and behavioral despair, hypothalamic orexin-serotonin dysregulation, increased hippocampal GABAergic signaling, and reduced HTR1A/HTR2A/BDNF/PSD95/p-ERK markers. The paradigm is proposed as a mouse model for noise-induced REM sleep disruption and mood deficits.

papers.title: From labels to latents: revealing state-dependent hippocampal computations and non-spatial replay with Jump Latent Variable Model.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: Introduces the Jump Latent Variable Model, an unsupervised latent-variable EM approach that infers population-activity latents and whether their dynamics are continuous or fragmented without external labels. Applied to rodent hippocampal recordings, it identified a continuity-fragmentation axis across sleep-wake states modulated by cholinergic input, revealed position-independent population patterns missed by supervised spatial decoding, and detected non-spatial pre-play and post-task replay events.

papers.title: iFLiP: accessible and low-cost lifetime fiber photometry for robust longitudinal and quantitative measurements of neural dynamics.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: Introduces iFLiP, a low-cost off-the-shelf fluorescence lifetime fiber photometry system with turn-key software that monitors lifetime changes up to 5000 Hz for days. Demonstrated utility by revealing striatal subregion- and cell-type-specific PKA dynamics during locomotion in mice and previously unappreciated PKA activity associated with sleep/wakefulness in the basal forebrain.

papers.title: Development of Circadian Circuitry Underlying Feeding-Fasting Rhythms in Drosophila Larvae.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: Characterizes the circuit driving development of feeding-fasting rhythms in early third instar Drosophila larvae, showing that inactivation of s-LNv circadian pacemakers and SIFamide neurons in the pars intercerebralis disrupts feeding rhythm development. The data indicate feeding rhythms emerge as s-LNv–SIFa connections form, and reduced pigment-dispersing factor (pdf) or SIFa signaling disrupts diurnal feeding and sleep differences.

papers.title: Housing mice in thermoneutrality causes peripheral tissue-specific changes in the number, identity, and phase of circadian-expressed mRNA transcripts.
papers.journal: American journal of physiology. Cell physiology
papers.summary: Used RNA sequencing of hearts, livers, and diaphragms sampled every 4 hours over 48 hours in constant darkness to test how thermoneutral versus room-temperature housing reshapes circadian gene expression in male mice. Thermoneutrality nearly quadrupled rhythmic transcripts in heart (11% to 42%) without changing liver proportion overall but with over 30% unique rhythmic transcripts and no detectable changes in core clock expression.

papers.title: Camus: a video-based framework for continuous behavioral monitoring in the mouse home-cage.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: Develops Camus, an open-source home-cage video monitoring platform using off-the-shelf USB cameras, infrared illumination, and 3D-printed components with a validated computer-vision model, recording up to 20 cages in parallel at ~$250 per cage. Camus captured circadian structure in locomotion, feeding, and drinking and revealed selective, age-progressive nesting deficits in transgenic 5xFAD mice.

papers.title: Assessing non-invasive glymphatic MRI markers following short-term sleep loss.
papers.summary: Examined non-invasive MRI glymphatic proxies (choroid plexus volume, perivascular space volume, free water index, DTI-ALPS) across habitual sleep, sleep restriction, and sleep deprivation in a large multi-site ENIGMA-sleep dataset (n=429). Sleep deprivation was associated with decreased PVSV and ALPS and increased FWI, while sleep restriction showed the inverse pattern; indices were largely uncoupled, suggesting they reflect distinct physiological processes.

papers.title: Autonomic and Cortical Signatures of Sleepiness After Prolonged Sleep Deprivation: Pupillary Reflex, Hippus Oscillations, and Visual Evoked Potentials.
papers.summary: Tracked pupillary light reflex, hippus oscillations, visual evoked potentials, and behavioral measures across 48-hour total sleep deprivation in 24 healthy adults. Found an organized biomarker profile including early PLR timing changes, decreased late redilation diameters, sustained elevation of absolute pupillary unrest, and delayed VEP component latencies, while brief tasks and resting cardiovascular measures stayed comparatively stable.

papers.title: Tumbly: An Open-Source Home-Cage Device for Time-Restricted Feeding in Mice.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: Describes Tumbly, an open-source, battery-powered, servo-driven food hopper for automated time-restricted feeding (TRF) in mouse home-cages with customizable faceplates. Validation across two institutions found 8-h TRF mice maintained body weight and ate similar amounts versus ad libitum, with no device failures over >1000 hours.

papers.title: A Benchmark of Unsupervised Circadian Phase Inference Methods for Bulk Transcriptomic Data.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: Benchmarked ten unsupervised circadian phase inference methods and two clock-gene baselines across 25 datasets (16 real, 9 simulated) using aligned circular MAE and secondary rhythm-reconstruction outcomes. CHIRAL had the lowest mean MAE (1.80 h), followed by clock-gene baselines (2.15–2.20 h) and TEMPO/CYCLOPS methods (2.49–2.80 h), with accuracy dependent on dataset and clock-gene rhythm strength.

papers.title: Sleep as a vulnerability marker in clinical high-risk populations. a multimodal systematic review.
papers.summary: PRISMA-based systematic review of 26 studies examining sleep across assessment modalities in clinical high-risk (CHR) populations. Sleep disturbances affected 59–80% of CHR individuals; polysomnographic markers (reduced prefrontal spindle duration, elevated NREM gamma power, reduced slow wave density) replicated across cohorts, and actigraphy predicted 12-month positive symptom worsening.

papers.title: EEG-SDL-Net: biomedical EEG signal classification via multi-level supervised Kolmogorov-Arnold networks.
papers.summary: Presents EEG-SDL-Net, a supervised deep learning framework combining 1D Sobel temporal enhancement, channel attention, Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks, and multi-level deep supervision for EEG signal classification. On SEED-VIG it achieved superior accuracy versus state-of-the-art methods and 15 ms real-time inference latency on a Raspberry Pi 4, with open-source code archived on Zenodo.

papers.title: Circadian phase alignment promotes survival under predictive oxidative stress.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: Used Synechococcus elongatus strains with altered free-running period to decouple circadian period from phase angle of entrainment across seasonal photoperiods. Strains whose stress-response programs peaked with the stressor outcompeted early- or late-peaking counterparts, and the wild-type period was uniquely plastic in aligning stress responses across all photoperiods.

papers.title: Functional and Structural Neuroanatomic Correlates of Intraoperative Anesthetic Dose-Adjusted EEG Alpha Power Among Older Surgical Patients.
papers.journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
papers.summary: In a prospective observational cohort (ALADDIN, n=168 older non-cardiac/non-cranial surgery patients), examined neuroanatomic correlates of intraoperative dose-adjusted frontoparietal EEG alpha power using preoperative MRI, MVPA, and CSF biomarkers. Lower dose-adjusted alpha power was linked to altered default mode/dorsal attention network connectivity and reduced cortical thickness, and was inversely associated with postoperative delirium severity.

papers.title: Wearable Technologies to Improve Physical Activity, Sedentary Breaks, Training, Sleep, and Safety: The ECSS-Wearable Technologies Special Interest Group Calls for Interdisciplinary Collaboration.
papers.summary: A position paper from the ECSS Wearable Technologies Special Interest Group reviewing applications of wearables across physical activity, sedentary behavior, training, sleep, and safety, while identifying critical challenges such as data quality, algorithm accessibility, interoperability, and user literacy. It calls for interdisciplinary collaboration, regulatory frameworks, open data infrastructure, and rigorous real-world intervention studies.

papers.title: Rapid Eye Movement Sleep Behavior Disorder as a Prodromal Manifestation of Alpha-Synucleinopathies.
papers.summary: Narrative review summarizing clinical features, mechanisms, biomarkers, and management of isolated REM sleep behavior disorder as a prodromal manifestation of alpha-synucleinopathies, emphasizing its long prodromal phase and its value as a model for early neurodegeneration. It discusses risk stratification tools (REM sleep without atonia quantification, dopamine transporter imaging, autonomic testing, alpha-synuclein seed amplification assays) and symptomatic treatments including clonazepam and melatonin.

papers.title: Intervention with Exogenous Melatonin Has No Adverse Effects on Cardiometabolic Parameters of Overweight Night Workers without Cardiometabolic Abnormalities.
papers.summary: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled crossover trial in 27 overweight night workers without cardiometabolic abnormalities tested 3 mg fast-release melatonin versus placebo (3 months, intermittent dosing on night-sleep days off). Melatonin produced no significant changes in cardiometabolic parameters compared with placebo, indicating no adverse cardiometabolic effects.

papers.title: Cardiac remodeling, autonomic parameters, and clinical factors associated with obstructive sleep apnea: a case-control study.
papers.summary: In a case-control study of 108 adults, OSA patients showed more cardiac remodeling (larger left atrial and right ventricular diameters, higher pulmonary artery systolic pressure, and more left ventricular hypertrophy, diastolic dysfunction, and tricuspid regurgitation), while the autonomic difference in RMSSD lost significance after multivariable adjustment. Obesity, smoking, ischemic heart disease, and left ventricular hypertrophy remained independently associated with OSA.

papers.title: Real-time wearable detection of respiratory infections in pediatric transplant households.
papers.journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
papers.summary: In a Phase IV trial cohort of 146 pediatric solid organ transplant recipients and household members, a resting heart rate-based real-time alerting algorithm was applied to detect respiratory virus infection, with 29 of 31 antigen-test outcomes (93.5%) corresponding to influenza, COVID, or other patient-reported symptoms. The authors describe heart rate, activity, and sleep/circadian features around alarm events as candidate features for algorithm improvement.

papers.title: Time-of-Day Variation in Airway Hyperresponsiveness in Asthma: Potential Circadian Mechanisms and Translational Implications.
papers.summary: This narrative review examines evidence on time-of-day variation in airway hyperresponsiveness in asthma, distinguishing clock-time variation from endogenous circadian regulation and discussing proposed mechanisms including neuroendocrine and autonomic gating, epithelial-immune coupling, airway smooth muscle reactivity, and redox regulation. It concludes that direct evidence for an intrinsic circadian rhythm of AHR in humans remains limited and that clock-targeted therapies remain investigational.

papers.title: Factors associated with postoperative sleep disturbance in patients undergoing thoracoscopic radical resection for lung cancer: a retrospective cohort study.
papers.summary: In a retrospective cohort of 62 patients undergoing thoracoscopic radical resection for lung cancer, 36 (58.1%) met criteria for postoperative sleep disturbance on postoperative day 2. Preoperative PSQI score (OR 1.58), intraoperative fluid volume (OR 1.004 per mL), and POD2 cough-induced pain (OR 2.23 per point) were independently associated with postoperative sleep disturbance.

papers.title: Artificial intelligence-generated and algorithmically personalized music interventions and their effects on brain function, behavior, and health: a critical review.
papers.summary: This critical review synthesized 21 studies (at least 1,005 participants) of algorithmically personalized and AI-generated music interventions, finding that closed-loop neural systems reported the most consistent neurophysiological signals and that all eight comparator studies favored the algorithmic condition, although evidence quality was very low and no finding was independently replicated. The evidence supports continued investigation but not clinical deployment.

papers.title: Longitudinal Pain Profiles and Their Clinical and Genetic Correlates in 624,996 U.S. Veterans.
papers.journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
papers.summary: In a Million Veteran Program cohort of 624,996 participants and 51.7 million outpatient pain ratings, Gaussian finite mixture modeling identified three longitudinal pain profiles: stable no pain, stable mild pain, and mild-to-moderate increasing pain. The increasing pain profile had markedly higher odds of chronic pain, opioid use disorder, opioid exposure, depression, and PTSD, and polygenic scores for depression, insomnia, ADHD, and tobacco use disorder were the most consistent predictors of increasing pain.

papers.title: The relationship between sleep problems and well-being among Chinese children: a moderated mediation model with anxiety as mediator and resilience as moderator.
papers.summary: In a cross-sectional study of 606 Chinese children (mean age 11.09 years), sleep problems were negatively correlated with well-being (r = -0.39), with anxiety mediating this association and resilience moderating the indirect effect, which was stronger in high-resilience children.

papers.title: Postoperative changes in primary monosymptomatic nocturnal enuresis following adenoidectomy or adenotonsillectomy in children with adenotonsillar hypertrophy and sleep-disordered breathing: A prospective cohort study.
papers.summary: In an uncontrolled prospective cohort of 140 children with primary monosymptomatic nocturnal enuresis and clinically diagnosed sleep-disordered breathing, adenoidectomy or adenotonsillectomy was associated with reduced median wet nights from 3 to 0 per week and 52.9% complete response at 3 months. The authors caution that the absence of a non-operative comparator prevents attribution of a surgery-specific treatment effect.

papers.title: Circadian blood pressure adaptation and arterial stiffness in pregnancy: An exploratory study.
papers.summary: In an exploratory study of 81 women using 24-hour ambulatory blood pressure monitoring, pregnant and nonpregnant women had comparable mean BP and Ambulatory Arterial Stiffness Index (AASI), but pregnancy showed reduced variability and a significant shift from dipper to non-dipper systolic pattern after 20 weeks' gestation.

papers.title: Perioperative non-invasive brain stimulation for the prevention of postoperative delirium: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials
papers.summary: This systematic review and meta-analysis of nine randomized controlled trials (1451 participants) found that perioperative non-invasive brain stimulation was associated with lower postoperative delirium risk (RR 0.41, 95% CI 0.31-0.56; moderate-certainty evidence), without reduced hospital stay; the authors conclude the evidence does not establish a class effect or support routine use.

papers.title: Efficacy and safety of commercial Chinese polyherbal preparations combined with biomedicine for elderly patients with primary insomnia: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
papers.summary: This systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials evaluated commercial Chinese polyherbal preparations combined with biomedicine versus biomedicine alone in elderly patients with primary insomnia, finding lower PSQI scores (MD = -2.09), a higher clinical effectiveness rate (RR = 1.21), and fewer adverse events (RR = 0.47). Evidence certainty was low to very low for efficacy, and P-curve analysis suggested insufficient evidential value for the clinical effectiveness rate despite strong evidential value for PSQI.

papers.title: Cognitive disengagement syndrome and alexisomia: examining the moderating role of anxiety-depression symptoms, stress, and insomnia symptoms among a sample of Lebanese adults.
papers.summary: In a cross-sectional study of 877 Lebanese adults, higher cognitive disengagement syndrome (CDS) traits were significantly associated with greater alexisomia; anxiety-depression and insomnia symptoms significantly moderated this association, attenuating it at higher symptom levels, whereas stress did not.

papers.title: Symptom and Quality-Of-Life Trajectories After High-Intensity Focused Ultrasound in Patients with Advanced Cancer: Exploratory Associations with Overall Survival in a Prospective Pilot Study.
papers.summary: This prospective pilot cohort study characterized symptom and quality-of-life trajectories in 54 patients with advanced cancer after high-intensity focused ultrasound, reporting that the most severe symptoms and global QoL reached their most favorable observed values at about one month post-HIFU. In exploratory univariable Cox analyses, back pain and hiccup at day 1 were associated with higher hazard of death, while higher global health status/QoL at day 1 was associated with lower hazard of death.

papers.title: Pain Management in Orthopedic Surgery: A Procedure-Specific Orthopedic-Anesthesia Approach to Perioperative Analgesia.
papers.summary: This narrative review synthesizes procedure-specific evidence on perioperative analgesia in orthopedic surgery, supporting multimodal analgesia and opioid-sparing NSAID use while noting that no universal regimen is justified and that benefits of regional techniques vary by procedure. It proposes a practical framework linking operation type, patient risk profile, analgesic options, and rehabilitation tasks, with unexpected severe pain prompting clinical reassessment rather than automatic escalation.

papers.title: Circadian Rhythm-Associated Diagnostic Biomarkers Reveal Immune Dysregulation and Molecular Subtypes in Recurrent Pregnancy Loss.
papers.journal: American journal of reproductive immunology (New York, N.Y. : 1989)
papers.summary: This bioinformatics study identified circadian rhythm-associated transcriptional alterations in recurrent pregnancy loss and nominated GJA1, UCP2, and GSN as candidate diagnostic biomarkers, with discovery-cohort AUCs of 0.80, 0.77, and 0.81 and independent-cohort AUCs of 0.72, 0.80, and 0.92. It further linked these biomarkers to immune infiltration changes and defined two molecular subtypes with distinct immune-stromal, coagulation, and metabolic features.

papers.title: A qualitative exploration of COPD lived experience, giving insight into symptom profile determinants and experiences of medical and non-medical interventions.
papers.journal: International journal of qualitative studies on health and well-being
papers.summary: This qualitative study using semi-structured interviews with 15 UK adults with COPD identified three themes: interconnected symptom experiences, navigating treatment uncertainty and burden, and becoming an active manager of COPD. Breathlessness was described as the most debilitating symptom, and participants reported frequent treatment changes, limited perceived medication effectiveness, and reliance on self-management strategies.

papers.title: Gut microbiome depletion aggravates glial-mediated Alzheimer's disease pathology through inflammatory, metabolic, and proteostatic dysregulation.
papers.summary: Using humanized Drosophila Alzheimer's disease models with glial transgene expression, this study found that antibiotic-induced gut microbiome depletion increased inflammatory signaling, impaired autophagy, lipid dysregulation, and accumulation of Aβ42 and phospho-tau, worsening sleep-circadian disruption and learning/memory deficits. The results identify the gut microbiome as a regulator of glial homeostasis and AD pathology via inflammatory, metabolic, and proteostatic pathways.

papers.title: Associations Between Psychological Factors, Routine Hematological and Biochemical Indicators, and Non-Suicidal Self-Injury Among University Students: An Exploratory Cross-Sectional Study.
papers.summary: In a cross-sectional study of 1,661 university students, routine hematological and biochemical indicators showed only weak associations with non-suicidal self-injury that did not survive FDR correction in adjusted models. Psychological factors yielded substantially better prediction (AUC 0.796) than routine indicators, and adding laboratory data did not improve prediction (AUC 0.787).

papers.title: EEG responses to monosodium glutamate concentration and individual umami sensitivity in healthy adults.
papers.summary: Combining psychophysics and 64-channel EEG in 38 healthy adults, this study found that increasing monosodium glutamate concentration reduced fronto-central P200 and posterior N200 amplitudes and altered beta-band orbitofrontal-dorsolateral prefrontal connectivity. EEG captured robust neural responses to MSG concentration, but individual umami sensitivity could not be decoded above chance.

papers.title: Cross-species multi-omics integration reveals lung alterations in acute kidney injury across mouse, pig, and human airway organoid models.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: Integrating clinical Epic Cosmos data with cross-species RNA-seq and proteomics from pig, mouse, and human airway organoid models, this study characterized acute kidney injury-associated lung alterations, showing higher mortality in the AKI-lung subgroup and a temporal shift from hyper-acute post-translational microvascular breakdown to transcriptional inflammatory and ER stress responses. Primary human donor lungs confirmed selective downregulation of CLOCK transcript in AKI.

papers.title: Adverse childhood experiences, lifestyle-related risks, and suicidal ideation and suicide attempts among Chinese college students: joint associations and exploratory network analysis.
papers.summary: In a cross-sectional survey of 18,723 Chinese college students, greater adverse childhood experience exposure and cumulative lifestyle-related risks were separately and jointly associated with higher prevalence of suicidal ideation and suicide attempts, with positive additive interaction (e.g., aPR 8.37 for SI and 10.30 for SA in the highest-risk combination). Exploratory network analysis highlighted poor sleep, emotional abuse, bullying, inadequate physical activity, and drinking as high-connectivity indicators.

topic.label: Sleep Homeostasis
topic.description: Sleep pressure, recovery, circadian interactions, and longitudinal regulation of NREM/REM sleep.
